name: Scientific Notation
description: Learn about Scientific Notation and its applications in physics.

content.overview: The mass of an electron is about 0.00000000000000000000000000000091 kg. Painful to even read, right? Scientific notation fixes that mess—it's just a compact, tidy way to write really huge or really tiny numbers so your eyes (and your calculator) don't have to suffer. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Scientific notation writes a number as (a number between 1 and 10) × 10^power {{viz:diagram-02}}
Positive exponents mean big numbers; negative exponents mean tiny numbers
The speed of light: 3 × 10⁸ m/s. An electron's mass: 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg
The exponent just counts how many places the decimal point moves
content.whyItMatters: Physics deals in extremes—from the size of the universe to the size of a proton. Scientific notation lets you write, compare, and calculate with these numbers without drowning in zeros. It's the difference between a clean, readable answer and a wall of digits nobody wants to check.
